By the Court:-
1. Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 21.02.2024 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Ranchi in connection with Jagarnathpur P.S. Case No. 43 of 2023, corresponding to G.R. No. 588 of 2024 whereby and where under, the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Ranchi, consequent upon the submission of the charge sheet against the petitioners, has taken cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/34 of Indian Penal Code and under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. The allegation against the petitioners is that the petitioner no.1 being the husband,
petitioner no.2 being the brother-in-law (dewar) and the petitioner no.3 being the mother-in-law of the informant- victim, in furtherance of their common intention, consequent upon the marriage of the informant-victim with the petitioner no.1, treated the informant-victim inhumanly, perpetrated mental cruelty upon her and abused her with obscene language, with the intention to force the informant-victim to bring dowry and to give in to the illegal demands of the petitioners.

In order to placate the petitioners, the father of the complainant paid Rs.50,000/- and the mother of the informant-victim also paid Rs.50,000/- additionally to the petitioners, but the same was not sufficient to satiate the greed of the petitioners.

The informant-victim was told by the petitioner no.3 to sever her relationship with her parents; because of non-fulfillment of the demand of dowry of the petitioners by them and the petitioner no.3 threatened the informant-victim to kill her by burning her and to get solemnized a second marriage of the petitioner no.1.

The petitioner no.2 in order to force the informant-victim to meet the illegal demand of dowry, whenever the informant used to be alone in her room, was trespassing to the room of the informant and was intending to molest the informant-victim with an evil intention.

On the informant-victim not acceding to the advances made by the petitioner no.2, the petitioner no.3 used to make false allegation against the informant-victim and the same was supported by the petitioner no.1.
The petitioner no.1 took the informant-victim to Bali in Indonesia as a conspiracy and assaulted the informant and treated her inhumanly and intimated the same to the petitioner nos.2 and 3.
The petitioner no.3 advised the petitioner no.1 to leave the opposite party no.2 at Bali and to come back alone to India.
The informant- victim was terrified and after much efforts and pleadings she was brought to Delhi.

The petitioner no.1 instructed the informant-victim to stop paying her educational loan, the EMI of which was deducted from the salary of the informant-victim and told the informant- victim to get the said EMI paid by her father.
The petitioner no.1 also demanded a new car and forced the informant-victim to give in to the demand of dowry of the new car or else she has to be treated with cruelty.

The petitioner no.1 forcibly made the informant-victim enter into an agreement to pay the house rent of their house Anjul Kumar Jha vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66600769/
2 from the bank account of the informant-victim after threatening the informant-victim to burn her alive unless she enters into the house rent agreement and pays the house rent.

sentences.text: Because of the ill-treatment as well as inhuman treatment, the informant-victim was under mental shock.

The petitioner no.3 also used to threaten the mother and father of the informant-victim; by telling that unless the new car is given by the mother of the informant-victim, her marriage with the petitioner no.1 will dissolved by a decree of divorce and the second marriage of the petitioner no.1 would be solemnized.

The informant- victim was not provided food and was kept hungry and ultimately the informant-victim was given shelter by the neighbour and she was rescued by her parents but in the process she was also physically assaulted.

4. On the basis of the written report submitted by the informant, police took up investigation of the case and the police found the allegation to be true during the investigation of the case and submitted charge sheet against the petitioners for having committed the offences punishable under Sections 498A/34 of Indian Penal Code as well as under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and consequently cognizance was taken.
5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the mediation has failed between the parties.

It is next submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that there was a compromise before the learned Judicial Commissioner,
Ranchi and consequent upon that the petitioners were granted bail.
Hence, because of compromise between the parties, the prayer as prayed for by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous petition be allowed.

6. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer made by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous petition.
It is categorically submitted by the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2
that there is no compromise entered into between the parties and the claim of compromise by the petitioners is a false one.

It is then submitted by the learned Addl. P.P. and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 that there is direct and specific allegation against each of the petitioners and the allegations were found to be true during the investigation of the case and since no compromise has been entered between the parties, so the sole ground for granting the relief prayed for in this criminal miscellaneous petition; being without any basis,
this criminal miscellaneous petition be dismissed.

7. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, this Court finds that the only ground for seeking the relief of quashing the order taking cognizance is that a compromise has been effected between the petitioners and the opposite party no.2 but the opposite party no.2 who is represented by his Advocate in this Court has categorically denied any compromise having been entered into between the parties.

sentences.text: After going through the materials in the record, this Court finds that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioners, which was found to be true during the investigation of the case and upon that the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance.
Since the sole ground for seeking relief in this criminal miscellaneous petition that a compromise has been effected is denied by the opposite party no.2

, hence, this Court is of the considered view that there is no justifiable reason to allow the prayer made by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous petition; in view of the direct and specific allegation against them, which was also found to be true during the investigation of the case.
9. Accordingly, this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit is dismissed.
